newsitem.title: USA: ITT says set to meet hotel margin goal.
newsitem.headline: ITT says set to meet hotel margin goal.

text.p: ITT Corp said it is on track to reach its goal of 30 percent margins at its hotels in 1997 following a 25 percent margin rate seen in the first quarter.

"North America continues to be a superb story with very little capital invested, while the rest of the world is achieving the kind of margins we hoped they would," ITT President Robert Bowman told analysts in a telephone conference call to discuss first quarter earnings.
ITT also said the hotel and casino giant has received expressions of buying interest for its Desert Inn casino from parties outside the casino industry.
Bowman said the company expects to reap about $400 million from the sale of the Desert Inn property in Las Vegas and its riverboat casino in Tunica, Miss.
The company also said it has received considerable buying interest for television station WBIS, which it jointly owns with Dow Jones & Co Inc.
ITT, which is fighting a hostile takeover attempt by rival Hilton Hotels Corp, is selling non-core assets in order to focus on its key hotel and casino businesses.
The company also said it anticipates longterm debt to be reduced to about $3.3 billion at the end of the second quarter from the first quarter level of $3.86 billion.
Bowman said ITT remains bullish on Las Vegas growth opportunities for the hotel and casino business.
He also noted that construction disruptions at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas are expected to peak in the second quarter. Disruptions from construction have cut into quarterly earnings.
